title: Assay Cupel Hearth
pages: Craft the controller from two bone blocks, a solar tempered plate from the Solar Smelter, two gold ingots, a Clay-Graphite Assay Crucible in the centre, two sealed steel plates and Cupel Tongs forged in the Coal Forge. Make the crucible by shaping a Green Assay Crucible (rows: clay/empty/clay; clay/coal or charcoal/clay; Screened Silica/clay/Screened Silica) and firing it in the Clinker Oven (220 ticks, 14 FE/t); the coal stands in for graphite and the silica for grog. The crucible holds the fusion charge before the bead is cupelled, so an unfired green crucible or a loose blast furnace item is refused in the craft. Place a blast furnace (any facing) directly beneath it, a bone block on each of its four diagonal corners at controller height, and an iron-bar post above each bone block. The bone ash holds the cupel while the raised cage contains the hot charge; a missing post stops the assay. Shared posts and cupels belong to the lower-position controller. It is a tier-5 device: its Assay Bead replaces the tungsten ingot in the Wire Drawing Bench recipe, whose Rhenium Filament leads on to the Enamel Kiln and the Heliostat Etcher.

Hold a raw metal batch in your main hand and right-click the formed controller. Each click loads one batch: the listed raw count and the listed experience levels (1 to 3), which the hearth condenses into an equal charge of Bottles o' Enchanting in its reagent slot. The batch then cupels over 40 ticks; click with an empty hand to collect the product, then the paired by-product metal. While a batch is buffered, a different raw metal is refused without cost. The assayer's judgement cannot be powered: with too few levels the hearth refuses and tells you how many are needed, without using anything. Inputs are item tags (forge:raw_materials/<metal>), so any mod's matching raw metal works. A missing bone block or blast furnace stops the hearth.

It runs 20 datapack cupellation recipes, each for a different raw metal, recovering a trace metal you would otherwise need a separate ore for. Three raw lead give 2 lead and 1 silver; nickel gives cobalt; platinum gives palladium; zirconium gives hafnium; tantalum gives two Tantalum Fluoride Concentrates plus niobium; fire each concentrate in the Kiln at 1000 heat for an ingot; osmium gives iridium; ruthenium gives rhodium; chromium gives vanadium; titanium gives zirconium; tungsten gives tin; antimony gives gold; thallium gives zinc; germanium gives gallium. Four raw zinc give 3 zinc and 1 indium; molybdenum gives rhenium; aluminum gives gallium; copper gives germanium; tin gives bismuth; iron gives manganese. Two raw gold give the Assay Bead plus 1 silver.

Automation: the formed hearth accepts tagged raw metal from the north or any input face and Bottles o' Enchanting in its second input slot, one bottle per listed level. It processes one batch every 40 ticks without drawing power; a blast furnace and four bone cupels with raised iron posts are its structural catalyst. The south face can be set to output by sneak-clicking it once with an empty hand; the bottom is output by default but blocked by the blast furnace. Extract the refined product and paired by-product from the two output slots. Empty-hand clicks collect product first, then by-product. The controller pauses when either output is full or the structure breaks. Manual assays pay player levels, which become the same bottle charge. When two recipes match, the lowest recipe id wins. Creative players assay without spending levels or materials. JEI's Cupellation category lists raw counts, tags, both outputs and the level cost, with the hearth as catalyst.
